title: Er is, er zijn — en deze, die, dit, dat
summary: Saying there is/are with er, and pointing with demonstratives tied to de/het

blocks.title: There is / there are: er is, er zijn
blocks.body: To say something exists, Dutch uses **er** + a form of *zijn*. One thing → *er is*; more than one → *er zijn*. It's the exact match for English 'there is / there are', and *er* is the little placeholder that makes it work.

rows: Er is een café in de straat.
There is a café on the street.

items.nl: Er is een winkel om de hoek.
items.en: There's a shop around the corner.
items.speak: Er is een winkel om de hoek.

blocks.prompt: Fill in: ___ vier fietsen voor de deur.
blocks.explain: Four bikes is plural, so *er zijn*. *Er is* would only fit one bike.

blocks.title: This and that: it depends on de or het
blocks.body: Dutch has four words for this/that, and which you pick depends on the noun's article. **de**-words take *deze* (this) and *die* (that). **het**-words take *dit* (this) and *dat* (that). So all that de/het work pays off again here.

blocks.explain: *huis* is a *het*-word, and 'this' for het-words is *dit*: *dit huis*. *deze/die* are only for de-words.
*deze kaas*. Because *kaas* is a de-word, 'this' is *deze*, not *dit*.

blocks.scene: At the market — Emma points things out at the cheese stall

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.nl: Kijk, deze kaas is echt lekker.
lines.en: Look, this cheese is really tasty.
lines.spotlight: *deze kaas* — de-word, so deze. And there's Emma's trademark *Kijk*.

lines.speaker: You
lines.spotlight: *dat brood* — het-word and far away, so dat.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.nl: Ook goed. En er zijn verse stroopwafels, hoor!
lines.en: Also good. And there are fresh stroopwafels, you know!
lines.spotlight: *er zijn* — plural, so *zijn*: pointing out what's on the stall.

blocks.prompt: Look around the room you're in. Write four sentences: two with *er is/er zijn*, and two pointing at objects with *deze/die/dit/dat*. Check each article first.
